findings.evidence: Page 3: "From a single token's cost to the fleet that carries it, every architectural decision can be traced — and defended — with arithmetic." and the title page (page 1) reads "First edition, 2026", while the copyright page (page 5) states "Edition identification. First edition, 2026 — build identifier v20260913; single evidence cutoff 2026-08-30." The PDF has 563 pages per the document metadata and the extracted page sequence runs to 563, yet the review prompt and the book's own citation style describe a 519-page work.
findings.issue: The physical extent of the document differs from the 519-page figure used to describe the book externally. The book's own internal pagination is self-consistent (front matter i–xiv, then chapters 1–26 at pages 1–4xx, appendices through the License at 538+), so the 563 PDF pages vs. 519 print pages is most likely PDF-vs-print pagination offset rather than a content defect. However, no note anywhere in the document reconciles the two extents, and any cross-reference to "the 519-page book" made by a reader against this PDF will not resolve.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a one-line note in the front matter (e.g., in the copyright or 'Edition identification' paragraph) stating the printed page count and that the PDF pagination differs (e.g., 'Print edition: 519 pages; PDF pagination adds N pages of front matter and figures'). If 519 is simply wrong, correct the external description instead.
